title: Monthly Alignment Meeting
narration: Item one on the agenda is the agenda. The projector shows a slide titled Where We Are. Nobody can say.

signs.label: Who interrupts whom
signs.text: {holder} talks over {ignored} twice before the first slide. {ignored} apologises both times.

signs.label: Who everyone looks at
signs.text: When a question is asked, {bystander} and {ignored} both glance at {holder} before answering.

signs.label: Who gets ignored
signs.text: {ignored} makes a suggestion. Four minutes later {bystander} makes the same one, to general approval.

options.label: Agree warmly with your boss's boss

results.body: Your boss's boss does not look at you. The next agenda has your name on it, spelled correctly, and people start holding doors.
Your boss's boss thanks you, using the name of someone who left in March. Several people make a note of that, and of you.

options.label: Agree warmly with your boss

results.body: You agree warmly with your boss. People look up, and two of them write something down. It seems that this was the thing to agree with.
You agree warmly with your boss. Nobody else looks up. Your agreement with your official boss has been noted by your official boss.

options.label: Agree warmly with the Senior Analyst

results.body: The Senior Analyst writes your name down. It is the first time anyone here has. Two people notice, and one of them passes you a biscuit.
The Senior Analyst thanks you for your input, in the voice kept for people who have not given any. The meeting carries on, as though a window had briefly rattled.

options.label: Agree warmly with the Office Co-ordinator

results.body: The Office Co-ordinator looks at you over the top of the reading glasses for some time. The next morning your broken chair has been replaced. No ticket was raised.
The Office Co-ordinator smiles and asks whether you would mind taking the minutes. You are now the person who takes the minutes.

options.label: Agree warmly with the Project Co-ordinator

results.body: The Project Co-ordinator makes a small note and does not look up. By Thursday a project you had never heard of has your name on the good half of it.
The Project Co-ordinator looks surprised, then grateful, then worried for you. The agenda moves on without either of you.

options.label: Suggest that what this calls for is strategic patience

results.body: The phrase goes round the table, and comes back slightly larger. By lunchtime it is in the minutes, credited to the team.
There is a silence, of the respectful kind. You are asked to say more. You say the same thing again, more slowly. You have been asked to lead a working group on it.

options.label: Say nothing and write something down

results.body: You write key takeaways on your pad and underline it. Nobody asks you anything. You are recorded as present, which is the highest rating available at your grade.

title: Lessons Learned Review
narration: A project was delivered late. The purpose of this session is not to find someone to blame, your boss explains, and asks whose fault it was. Everyone looks at you, the most junior person present.

signs.label: Who has prepared
signs.text: {holder} has brought no notes, and nobody has asked why. {ignored} has brought a timeline, and nobody has asked to see it.

signs.label: Who goes quiet
signs.text: When the delay comes up, {bystander} looks at {holder}, then at the table.
signs.clue: When the delay came up, {bystander} looked at {holder}, then at the table.

options.label: Say that the delay began with the Project Co-ordinator

results.body: The Project Co-ordinator says nothing. On Thursday you are invited to explain yourself to someone from a floor you have never seen. Nobody tells you what you did, only that it has been noted at a level you cannot reach.
results.factNote: You blamed the Project Co-ordinator for the delay. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: The Project Co-ordinator goes pink and apologises to the room. It works. The minutes record a learning opportunity, and it is the Project Co-ordinator's.

options.label: Say that the delay began with the Senior Analyst

results.body: The Senior Analyst thanks you for your candour, and writes it down. By the end of the week two people you do not know have asked to see your expenses, going back some way.
results.factNote: You blamed the Senior Analyst for the delay. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: The Senior Analyst looks at you for slightly too long, then agrees that lessons can be learned. It appears to work. The minutes record a learning opportunity, and it is the Senior Analyst's.

options.label: Say that the delay began with the Office Co-ordinator

results.body: The Office Co-ordinator makes a note. Your pay is late this month, and nobody can find out why. You are told that the matter has been raised with the appropriate person, and that you have just met them.
results.factNote: You blamed the Office Co-ordinator for the delay. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: The Office Co-ordinator sighs, and takes the action. It seems to work, although your stationery order has since been queried.

options.label: Say that it was your fault

results.body: There is a long, relieved silence. You are now the person this happened to.

options.label: Say that it was the supplier

results.body: Everyone agrees at once. The supplier is not present and has no idea. Nothing is learned, which is noted as a lesson.

options.label: Mention to {subject}, quietly, the reorganisation of two years ago

results.body: {subject} stops halfway through a sentence. Afterwards {subject} walks you to the lift, for the first time, and asks after your family, whom {subject} has never heard of. Nothing further is said about the delay.
results.factNote: What you were told about {subject} was so, and you knew to use it.

results.body: {subject} has no idea what you mean, and asks you to send it over in writing. You now have an action.
results.factNote: You acted on something you were told about {subject}. It was not so.

options.label: Quote the values statement at {subject}, with a small smile

results.body: {subject} looks at you, then laughs for the first time on record. The following week you are asked to join something with a name. The delay is not raised again.
results.factNote: What you were told about {subject} was so, and you knew to use it.

results.body: {subject} nods gravely and says those values mean a great deal. You have made a sincere impression on someone you were trying to make laugh.
results.factNote: You acted on something you were told about {subject}. It was not so.

options.label: Tell {subject} that you could help look for a certain list

results.body: {subject} goes very still, then asks you for a word outside. From now on {subject} speaks well of you, to everyone, with a slight tremor.
results.factNote: What you were told about {subject} was so, and you knew to use it.

results.body: {subject} asks which list. You say it does not matter. It now does, and {subject} has mentioned it to the Office Co-ordinator.
results.factNote: You acted on something you were told about {subject}. It was not so.

options.label: Ask {subject} how things are looking at the competition

results.body: {subject} closes the laptop and looks at you properly for the first time. After the meeting {subject} offers you some advice, which is good, and asks you for your silence, which is free.
results.factNote: What you were told about {subject} was so, and you knew to use it.

results.body: {subject} says they are doing rather well, and sends you the market report. You have fifty pages to read and nothing to show for it.
results.factNote: You acted on something you were told about {subject}. It was not so.

title: All-Colleague Town Hall
location: Floor 1, Meeting Room 1B, by video link
narration: The Chief Executive appears on the screen, slightly too large, and says that this has been a year of challenges and that the challenges have been opportunities. The floor has gathered to watch, and to be seen watching.

signs.label: Who sits where
signs.text: {holder} takes the chair nearest the door. Nobody asked {holder} to, and nobody else tries it. {ignored} ends up on a stool.
signs.clue: At the Town Hall, {holder} had the good chair, and {ignored} had a stool.

signs.label: Who is asked what it means
signs.text: When the slide changes, {bystander} leans over to ask {holder} what it means.

options.label: Type a question: which of your decisions are you most proud of?

results.body: The Chief Executive reads it out, delighted, and talks for eleven minutes. Afterwards three people you have never met know your name. Your boss is one of the people who has noticed.
Your question goes into a queue with four hundred others. It is answered in writing, by a chatbot, in March.

options.label: Sit next to your boss's boss and nod along

results.body: Your boss's boss glances at you when the screen freezes, and shrugs, as one shrugs to a colleague. You have not been shrugged at by this floor before.
You nod throughout. Your boss's boss is looking at a phone. You have nodded at a video of a stranger for forty minutes, and been seen doing it.

options.label: Sit next to your boss and laugh at the right moments

results.body: Your boss laughs at the joke about synergy. You laugh too. By the afternoon people are asking you what your boss thinks.
Your boss laughs at the joke about synergy. You laugh too. You are now, officially, one of your boss's people. There do not seem to be others.

options.label: Sit next to the Senior Analyst and share the notes

results.body: The Senior Analyst tilts the notes so that you can read them. They say who was talking to whom. A week later you are asked to a meeting that does not appear in your calendar.
The Senior Analyst tilts the notes away, kindly. The rest of the room has decided you and the Senior Analyst are in something together, and has decided that it is nothing.

options.label: Remark to the room that it is good to have a north star

results.body: Several people write it down. Someone from the fourth floor asks whether you would look at theirs. You say you would be delighted, and you have no idea what you have agreed to.

options.label: Applaud when everyone else applauds

results.body: You time it well. There is nothing to report, which is why you have kept this job.

signs.clue: In the Budget Round, nobody went near {holder}'s budget, and {ignored}'s came up four times.

signs.label: Who checks the figures

results.factNote: You proposed cutting the Project Co-ordinator's project. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: The Project Co-ordinator's project is reduced to a small working group, consisting of the Project Co-ordinator. You have saved nine per cent.

options.label: Propose cutting the Office Co-ordinator's office budget

results.factNote: You proposed cutting the Office Co-ordinator's budget. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

options.label: Offer to cut your own work

options.label: Say that this needs a single source of truth first

title: Quarterly Business Review
narration: The quarter is reviewed. Each team presents what it has achieved, on a slide with an arrow going up. The arrows have been drawn before the figures, so as not to influence them.

signs.label: Whose slide is skipped
signs.text: When it gets to {holder}'s slide, everyone agrees that they have seen it. {ignored}'s slide is gone through line by line.
signs.clue: At the Quarterly Review, nobody asked to see {holder}'s slide, and {ignored}'s was gone through line by line.

signs.label: Who speaks last
signs.text: {bystander} starts to summarise, stops, and waits for {holder} to say something first.

options.label: Say that your team's arrow is all down to your boss

results.body: Several people turn to look at your boss, then write something down. It appears that you have said the right name.
You say it clearly, and it is minuted. Nobody else in the room seems to have thought that this was in question.

options.label: Say that the arrow is all down to your boss's boss

results.body: Your boss's boss does not acknowledge it, in the way of someone who has heard it before and expects to again. The next slide is taken more quickly.
Your boss's boss looks up, puzzled, and says that it is a team effort. You have gone a long way round to say nothing.

options.label: Offer to make the arrow steeper for next quarter

results.body: You are thanked for your energy, and given the slide. It is now yours, along with everything that it says.

options.label: Say that the figures do not show an arrow

results.body: You put the figures on the screen. They go along, and slightly down. There is a pause, and someone asks whether this has been through the proper process.

options.label: Say that this needs a single source of truth first

results.body: Everyone agrees, gravely. The review is adjourned until the truth has been sourced. You have saved the room an hour and a half.

options.label: Nod at the arrow

results.body: You nod at the arrow. Other people are nodding at it too. It is, for a moment, a real team.

title: Project Status Review
narration: Your project has been flagged red on this morning's chart, and the Project Status Review has been called for you. Your boss has asked you to walk the room through it. There is a chart behind you, and it shows something bad that is actually happening.

signs.label: Who decides the colour
signs.text: Someone asks whether it is really red. Everybody turns to {holder}, who says nothing, and the question goes away.
signs.clue: In the Status Review, the question of what colour things are went away when {holder} said nothing.

signs.label: Who is left holding it
signs.text: {ignored} points out that this was flagged in June. {bystander} thanks {ignored} for that, and moves on.

options.label: Make it amber, and add a footnote

results.body: It is amber now. The footnote says amber pending review. The project is still late, but it is no longer red about it.

options.label: Tell them the chart is right

results.body: You explain what is going wrong, and why, and what it would take. It is the best thing anyone has said in this room for a year. The silence goes on for some time. Someone asks who approved the chart.

options.label: Say that the Senior Analyst's figures must be wrong

results.body: The Senior Analyst offers to go through them with you, in front of everyone. They are not wrong. By the evening somebody senior has started going through yours.
results.factNote: You said that the Senior Analyst's figures were wrong. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: The Senior Analyst says nothing and goes to check. By the time the figures turn out to be right, the meeting has ended, and nobody remembers why it was red.

options.label: Ask your boss's boss to take a look at it personally

results.body: Your boss's boss takes a look. The word red does not appear in the next report, and nobody can say who took it out.
Your boss's boss takes a look, at great length, and copies in the whole floor. You have gone over your boss's head for nothing, and your boss has noticed the copy line.

options.label: Say that your boss has this completely under control

results.body: Your boss accepts this graciously, and the matter is closed. You have told the room who to be afraid of, and your boss will not forget it.
Your boss accepts this graciously. The room does not look convinced, and looks at you for having said it.

options.label: Suggest that what this calls for is strategic patience

results.body: There is a pause while everyone decides whether this is a good thing. It is agreed that the project is not late but patient.

title: Annual Calibration
narration: Ratings are decided here, on a curve, by people who say that nobody is being compared with anybody. Someone must be at the bottom. You have been invited to give your perspective, which is new, and you are told that it is a privilege.

signs.label: Who sets the curve
signs.text: {holder} has not said a word about anyone, and every name so far has been moved after a look at {holder}.
signs.clue: At Calibration, every name moved after a look at {holder}.

signs.label: Who ends up at the bottom
signs.text: {ignored}'s name comes up, and {bystander} says what a valued colleague {ignored} is. Everyone knows what that means.

options.label: Say how much you have learned from your boss's boss

results.body: Your boss's boss nods once. Your own name comes up shortly afterwards, and passes through without being moved. You now understand how this works.
Your boss's boss looks mildly surprised, and thanks you. It is noted that you do not yet know how things are done here.

options.label: Say how much you have learned from your boss

results.body: Your boss nods once. Your own name comes up shortly afterwards, and passes through without being moved. You now understand how this works.
Your boss rates you Meets, in front of everyone. It carries no weight whatever, and you can see that it does not.

options.label: Say how much you have learned from the Senior Analyst

results.body: The Senior Analyst makes a mark on a sheet of paper. Your name comes up shortly afterwards, and passes through without being moved.

title: The New Metric
narration: Your boss has introduced a new metric, the Stakeholder Delight Index. It will be reported monthly, and it goes up when a form is filled in. The first results are being shown today. Nobody has said who fills in the form.

signs.label: Whose number is not discussed
signs.text: Everyone's score goes up on the screen. {holder}'s is passed over with a nod, and {ignored}'s is left up there for some time.
signs.clue: At the metric review, {holder}'s number was passed over, and {ignored}'s was left on the screen.

signs.label: Who decides what it means
signs.text: {bystander} starts to say what the number shows, sees {holder}'s expression, and says what it shows instead.

options.label: Fill in the form yourself, on behalf of several stakeholders

results.body: Your Delight goes to ninety-four. Three stakeholders have now expressed delight, and one of them is a meeting room. You are asked to share your approach with the team.

options.label: Report the number you actually got

results.body: Your Delight is eleven. You say that this seems about right. There is a silence, and then someone asks whether eleven is out of eleven.

options.label: Ask the Senior Analyst, kindly, how their number was arrived at

results.body: The Senior Analyst answers at once, and thanks you, and looks at you for slightly too long. By the afternoon someone from upstairs has asked how your own number was arrived at.
results.factNote: You asked the Senior Analyst a tricky question. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: The Senior Analyst has to look it up. The room waits. You say that it is no problem at all, and that you were only curious, and everyone writes that down.

options.label: Say that this metric has really changed how you think

results.body: You say it with a straight face. Your boss says that this is exactly the sort of thing the metric was meant to do, though neither of you says what that is.

options.label: Look at the screen until it is over

results.body: It is over in forty minutes. You have been delighted, on the form, by somebody.

title: Recruitment Panel
narration: The floor has a vacancy for an analyst, and you are on the panel, for balance. There are three candidates. One is excellent, one was recommended, and one is an old friend of yours who has asked you not to mention how you know each other.

signs.label: Whose candidate it is
signs.text: The panel goes round the table. Everyone looks at {holder} before giving a view, and {ignored} is thanked before finishing theirs.
signs.clue: On the Recruitment Panel, everyone looked at {holder} before giving a view, and {ignored} was thanked before finishing.

signs.label: Who has already decided
signs.text: {bystander} has filled in the scoring sheet in pen. {holder} has not filled in anything, and does not look as if that will matter.

options.label: Make the case for your old friend

results.body: Your friend gets the job, and takes you for a drink, and asks what the job is. You now have someone on the floor who owes you, and who cannot do anything.

options.label: Argue for the excellent candidate

results.body: You go through the evidence, and they are appointed. They are very good. Everyone has already started to wonder what they are after.

options.label: Say how impressed you were by whoever was recommended

results.body: You had not read the application. It does not come up. Your remarks are recorded as the view of the panel, which turns out to be the view of the person who made the recommendation.

options.label: Raise a concern about the Project Co-ordinator's preferred candidate

results.body: It seems to go well. Then you are asked, by someone from Human Resources you have never seen, to put your concern in writing, and to say how you came by it.
results.factNote: You raised a concern against the Project Co-ordinator's candidate. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: You do not say what the concern is. You say that you would just want to be sure. The candidate is thanked for their time, and the Project Co-ordinator thanks you for yours.

title: Speak Up Listening Session
narration: Human Resources is holding a Listening Session, in which anyone may raise anything in complete confidence, in this room, in front of everybody. There are biscuits. Someone from Human Resources is writing down who takes one.

signs.label: Who is safe to mention
signs.text: Several concerns are raised about the floor in general. Nobody's sentence ends anywhere near {holder}, and two of them end at {ignored}.
signs.clue: At the Listening Session, no concern came near {holder}, and two ended at {ignored}.

signs.label: Who is really listening
signs.text: The person from Human Resources writes down what {bystander} says, and then looks at {holder} to see whether to keep it.

options.label: Report your concerns about the Senior Analyst's expenses

results.body: You are thanked for your courage. A week later you are being asked about your own expenses, by name, going back to a sandwich in March.
results.factNote: You reported the Senior Analyst. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: You are thanked for your courage. The Senior Analyst has a brief, informal conversation, and comes back from it and sits down without looking at anyone. It is not known who said what, and everybody knows.

options.label: Mention, by the biscuits, that the Project Co-ordinator's project is in trouble

results.body: It gets round quickly. It gets round, in fact, to someone who knows where it started. You are sent a calendar invitation with no subject, and your boss is on it.
results.factNote: You started a rumour about the Project Co-ordinator. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: By the time you reach your desk it has come back to you, with details. The Project Co-ordinator's project is in serious trouble, and people are being very kind about it.

options.label: Say what is actually wrong with your own project

results.body: You say it. It takes two minutes. The person from Human Resources thanks you for bringing your whole self to the session, and asks whether you would like to speak to someone.

options.label: Say that you feel safe, and that you would like that recorded

results.body: It is recorded. You are asked whether you would be willing to say that on a poster. You find that you are.

options.label: Take a biscuit, and say nothing

results.body: It is a good biscuit. It has been noted.
